history.origins: Busca is a variation of CiapanÃ² (also known as Rovescino, Traversone, or Tressette a non Prendere), a reverse trick-taking game from Lombardy, Italy. CiapanÃ² was very popular in Lombardy until the 1980s and is still played there.
timeline: Traditional origins: CiapanÃ² played for generations in Lombardy
1980s: Peak popularity of CiapanÃ² in Lombardy
Modern era: Busca variation documented by Davide Gullo
Contemporary: Still played in Italian regions
history.cultural: Busca and related games like CiapanÃ² are part of Italian regional card game traditions. The Milanese dialect name 'CiapanÃ²' translates roughly to 'Don't catch it!' reflecting the reverse nature of the game.
history.evolution: Busca modifies CiapanÃ² scoring by multiplying all points by three and introducing the special Pita card (Ace of Coins worth 8 points). The objective shifts from simply avoiding points to taking at least one but not the most.

setup.deck: 40-card pack: Italian suits (swords, batons, cups, coins) or Milanese/French suits (spades, clubs, hearts, diamonds). Cards rank: 3 (high), 2, Ace, King, Horse/Queen, Jack/Fante, 7, 6, 5, 4 (low).
setup.dealing: Deal 10 cards to each player (anticlockwise). Turn to deal passes to the right after each hand.
setup.equipment: 40-card Italian or Milanese pack, score sheet for tracking busche

rules.objective: Take at least one point but avoid taking the most points. Players who take no points or the most points score penalty points called busche.
rules.gameplay: No trumps. Player to dealer's right leads first. Any card may be led; others must follow suit if possible. Highest card of led suit wins trick; winner leads to next. It is illegal to lead coins in the first trick. The Pita (Ace of Coins) cannot be discarded in the first trick if unable to follow suit.
keyRules: Cannot lead coins on first trick
Pita (Ace of Coins) cannot be discarded first trick if void
Goal: take â‰¥1 point but not most points
Penalties called 'busche' for taking 0 or most points

strategy.basic: Try to win exactly one low-value trick to avoid zero points. Avoid winning high-value cards (Pita, Aces, last trick). If you have the Pita, plan carefully as it's worth 8 points.
strategy.intermediate: Track which suits opponents are void in. Use the restriction on leading coins early to your advantage. Count points taken by each player to predict who is at risk of most/least points.
strategy.advanced: Manipulate trick distribution to ensure you take some but not most points. Force opponents to take the Pita or last trick. Coordinate indirectly with other players to 'cover' (coprire) and prevent someone from getting zero points.
tips: Taking exactly one low-point trick is ideal
Avoid the Pita (Ace of Coins) - it's worth 8 points
The last trick is worth 3 points - factor this into calculations
If you have no points late in the hand, try to win any trick to avoid 1 busca penalty
If leading and have many points, consider giving tricks to players who already have points
Watch for opportunities to force the Pita on specific opponents

variations.name: Kifameno (Who Wins Least)
variations.description: Kifameno is a Slovenian losing Tressette variant where 2–4 players are dealt 10 cards each and undealt cards form a draw stack that is used between tricks.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This Slovenian variant changes player counts and introduces drawing from a stock; it is recorded here as a related game but its engine changes are not yet encoded as overrides.

scoring.description: Penalty points called busche accumulate from deal to deal. Card points in tricks are converted into busche based on how many points each player has and whether anyone took no points or the most points.
scoring.winCondition: Over several deals, the player with the lowest total busche wins the match; players taking no points or the most card points in a deal gain busche according to the Busca schedule.
